key: And he hath coined for Us a similitude, and hath forgotten the fact of his creation, saying: Who will revive these bones when they have rotted away?
s: After man, made from a drop, is called an open opponent, the ayah gives his challenge; Ibn Kathir, on 36:77 to 36:80, reads it, whether Ubayy ibn Khalaf or al-ʿAs ibn Wa’il occasioned it, as meant for every denier of the resurrection.

evidence.words: وَعَلَى كُلِّ تَقْدِيرٍ سَوَاءً كَانَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتُ قَدْ نَزَلَتْ فِي أُبي بْنِ خَلَفٍ، أَوْ [فِي] الْعَاصِ [بْنِ وَائِلٍ] ، أَوْ فِيهِمَا، فَهِيَ عَامَّةٌ فِي كُلِّ مَنْ أَنْكَرَ الْبَعْثَ. وَالْأَلِفُ وَاللَّامُ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الإنْسَانُ﴾ لِلْجِنْسِ، يَعُمُّ كُلَّ مُنْكِرٍ لِلْبَعْثِ.
evidence.gloss: On every reckoning, whether these ayahs came down about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, or about al-ʿAs ibn Wa’il, or about both, they are general, for everyone who denies the resurrection. The article in His saying “Hath not man seen” is for the kind: it takes in every denier of the resurrection.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Ya-Sin 36:78, at 3782). Ibn Kathir’s one comment on 36:77 to 36:80 gives the occasion (Ubayy ibn Khalaf, or al-ʿAs ibn Wa’il, crumbling a rotted bone; he rejects the Abdullah ibn Ubayy report since the surah is Meccan), then says that on every reckoning the ayahs are general for every denier of the resurrection. Further on, glossing 36:78, he says the denier forgot that God made him from nothing. Both are his, but they stand far apart in the comment with hadith between, and the proposer’s evidence joined them with an ellipsis, which cannot be re-found as one verbatim run. CHANGED the reading to the contiguous passage alone (dropping the clause on being made from nothing, naming the two men he gives for “whichever scoffer”), and replaced the evidence with that run as the packet prints it. 42 words; entry-check ok.
